title: Tupi-Guarani expansion
summary: Speakers of Tupi languages spread outward from a homeland in the Madeira-Guapore region of the Amazon, and the Tupi-Guarani branch occupied areas of southern and southeastern Brazil and the eastern coast. One source dates the expansion to about 6,000 to 2,000 years ago and calls it among the largest and most successful continental-scale migrations; the people made ceramics and farmed. The exact homeland and dates are disputed.

uncertainty.note: Sources give "years ago", not calendar years: about 6,000 to 2,000 years ago for the expansion, and 2,800-3,000 years ago for the origin of the Tupi family. Start and end here are rounded to -4000 and 0 for the 6,000-2,000 range and are approximate. The id year 0500 does not come from either source.

beats.caption: Tupi speakers disperse from the Madeira-Guapore homeland toward the southeast and south of Brazil.
Skilled farmers who made ceramics, they turned forest into productive land.
The expansion is described as one of the largest and most successful migrations identified at the continental level.

reviewer_note: Least sure: dating. Sources disagree (6,000-2,000 years ago expansion; 2,800-3,000 years ago family origin), the homeland is disputed (Madeira-Guapore vs the Madeira-Amazon confluence), and the id year 0500 is not supported by either source. Waypoint order is geographic, not a dated itinerary. The Brazilian East coast is named by the source but not pinned. Conexoes Amazonicas has no named author; class other.
